artifacts.summary: 5-phase, 4.5-hour plan extending plan-file-scope-harvest.sh with a capability-gated post-processing stage that appends the generated surfaces any .lean edit forces (status.typ, ancestor-chain inventory READMEs, two narrow-glob typst surfaces), with 11 new regression cases and precedent-plan replay verification.

memory_candidates.content: When a repo-wide derived artifact (a generated status table, a generated inventory block in a README) is appended to a task's file_scope because an edit mechanically forces its regeneration, that append is also read by the territory/overlap machinery (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's file_scope_collision check and task-lock.sh, both splicing scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh). Any two concurrent tasks whose edits force the same shared generated surface therefore collide and serialize. This is usually the correct outcome -- they genuinely fight the same pre-commit gate over the same file -- but it is an invisible second-order consequence of a scope-completeness fix, and file_scope is a flat array of strings with no per-entry provenance or exclusivity annotation, so a 'shared, non-exclusive' marking is not expressible without a schema change. Decide the parallelism trade-off explicitly at plan time rather than discovering it as an unexplained DEFER.
